description: Meetings with the signals the promoter's extractor returned for them (type, content, self-reported confidence, owner as written, entity names) and gold labels for what each signal is. scripts/eval_signal_triage.py rebuilds each signal with the promoter's own heuristics (tier from confidence < 0.7, first-name owner match, lone-client scope), runs signal_promotion_triage, and scores heuristics vs the model vs gold. gold.type may list also_ok_type for a genuinely ambiguous signal; gold.firmness is set only for decisions; gold.owner / gold.client are a name or null, with also_ok_<field> for a defensible alternative (the cadence of a client's own sync may count as that client's). The damaging errors are a proposal promoted to a firm decision, work assigned to the wrong person, and a client stamped on an internal signal.
provenance: Synthetic. Failure types taken from the signal promoter's heuristics (app/services/signal_promoter.py) and from signals observed on a production KB (2026-09): first-name owner collisions, options under discussion stored as decisions, a meeting's lone client stamped on internal items, status facts recorded as decisions. Names and details invented. Labels authored with the triage operation and not independently reviewed (also_ok_client on m01 was added after the first run); treat as a smoke test, not a benchmark.
